what_it_is: AI Security Platform: Guardrails, Red Team, AI Gateway with MCP gateway, Workforce AI Security.
identity_note: F5 AI Guardrails and AI Red Team come from CalypsoAI, now part of F5. F5 docs and the Python SDK still use the CalypsoAI name.

1.reason: Workforce AI Security inventories AI services, models and MCP servers from network traffic. No cloud posture checks.
1.evidence: Passively identify all AI usage, including sanctioned apps, private models, and shadow AI, across the entire network.
1.has: Workforce AI Security (SurePath AI) passive network discovery of AI apps, models, MCP servers.
1.lacks: Network-only discovery. No cloud-account inventory, endpoint or browser discovery, or AI posture checks.

2.reason: MCP Gateway registers MCP servers and sets per-tool allow and deny lists. Guardrails block unauthorized tool calls.
2.evidence: MCP Server Registry provides a centralized, single-pane view of every MCP server across your environment
2.has: MCP Gateway with server registry and per-tool allow lists. Google Agent Gateway integration.
2.lacks: Early-access sign-up still listed for AI Gateway. One named agent platform. No sandbox.

3.reason: Guardrails log every enforcement action, export to SIEM and fail closed. Red Team findings feed guardrails automatically.
3.evidence: Explain and trace every enforcement action with detailed analysis and guardrail attribution.
3.has: Audit logs and SIEM export. Fail-closed inline blocking. AI Remediate pushes findings to guardrails.
3.lacks: No named SIEM or ITSM integration found. Blocks prompts and tool calls, not hosts.

4.reason: Guardrails block injection, jailbreak, PII and toxic output via API, SDK, AI Gateway and NGINX Gateway Fabric.
4.evidence: Protect against prompt injection attacks, data exfiltration, and jailbreak attacks without excessive false positives.
4.has: AI Guardrails: SaaS API and SDK, AI Gateway, NGINX Gateway Fabric, Google Agent Gateway.

5.reason: Guardrails ship EU AI Act, GDPR and HIPAA templates. Red Team reports show OWASP LLM Top 10 results.
5.evidence: automated auditing templates for GDPR, HIPAA, EU AI Act, and more
5.has: Audit logs, EU AI Act and GDPR templates, OWASP LLM Top 10 reports.
5.lacks: No AIBOM export. NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001, MITRE ATLAS mapping not found.

6.reason: AI Red Team runs signature, operational and multi-turn agentic attacks via UI, API and SDK, with OWASP-mapped reports.
6.evidence: The AI Security Red-Team agent acts autonomously, creating and sending prompts based on a user-defined malicious intent.
6.has: AI Red Team: 10,000+ monthly attack patterns, agentic warfare, API and SDK, CI/CD re-testing.

7.reason: MCP Gateway applies per-tool access control and records which agent acted and for whom. No NHI governance found.
7.evidence: Complete tool-call audit trail captures every invocation with full context
7.has: AI Gateway RBAC with per-tool allow and deny lists and a central agent registry.
7.lacks: No per-agent cryptographic identity. No API key, service account or OAuth grant discovery found.

8.reason: No model file, dataset or AI code scanning found. Guardrails inspect retrieved context at runtime only.
8.evidence: Searches run: F5 model file scanning Hugging Face malicious model pickle backdoor scan | F5 AI Security Platform model scanning dataset PII poisoning AI SAST code scanning | F5 AI security posture management CI/CD supply chain scanning
8.lacks: No model scanner, dataset checks or AI SAST in F5 AI Security Platform pages.

notes: F5 completed the CalypsoAI acquisition (F5 blog: F5 completes acquisition of CalypsoAI, introduces F5 AI Guardrails and F5 AI Red Team). F5 announced the SurePath AI acquisition and the F5 AI Security Platform on 2026-06-23. SurePath AI powers Workforce AI Security, which is network-based discovery with no agents or extensions. F5 introduced the AI Gateway with Model Gateway, MCP Gateway and Guardrails on 2026-08-18, and an AI Gateway early-access sign-up page is still live, so MCP Gateway and per-tool controls are scored partial. F5 AI Guardrails integrates with Google Cloud Agent Gateway (2026-05-06), Red Hat OpenShift AI and NGINX Gateway Fabric. Red Team reports added OWASP LLM Top 10 2026 attack success rates on 2026-09-30. CI/CD re-testing is described in an F5 blog as something customers build, and no native scheduler was found. SIEM export is stated without naming a SIEM. BIG-IP, NGINX, F5 WAF, Distributed Cloud API Security, Bot Defense and Web App Scanning protect AI app endpoints and APIs, and none is one of the 8 AI modules. F5 named a Market Shaper in the 2026 Gartner Emerging Market Quadrant for AI Application Security. Unsure points: 6.3 scored yes on the CI/CD blog plus OWASP-mapped reports. 7.1 scored partial because the audit trail records on whose behalf an agent acted, which points to delegated user identity. Module 8 scored no after 3 searches, and the solutions page mentions supply chain risk only in general terms.
